title: Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) for Spaceflight Life Support
measuredFact: Standard NASA planning reference rates: Oxygen consumption is 0.84 kg/person/day; nutritional dry food solids requirement is 0.62 kg/person/day; direct drinking water requirement is 1.62 kg/person/day (hygiene and food preparation add approximately 1.0–1.5 L/person/day, totaling ~2.5–3.5 L/person/day).
gameAssumption: Outpost baseline for 4 crew: 3.2 kg O₂/day (0.80 kg/person), 12 L total potable water/day (3.0 L/person combining drinking and hygiene), and 6 kg wet food rations/day (1.5 kg/person rehydrated).
simplificationRationale: Rounds numbers to clean decimals for junior astronaut cognitive accessibility while preserving physiological mass conservation. Total potable water is a game assumption inspired by, but not directly equivalent to, BVAD sub-allocations.

title: Oxygen Generation System (OGS) Flight Performance & Water Electrolysis Stoichiometry
authorOrMission: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center & ISS ECLSS Office
measuredFact: Water electrolysis converts deionized water into oxygen and hydrogen via 2 H2O -> 2 H2 + O2. Mass stoichiometry requires 1.125 kg of water per 1.0 kg of O2 produced (36.015 g H2O / 31.998 g O2). Operating cell power demand is ~4.0–6.0 kWh per kg O2.
gameAssumption: Generating 3.2 kg of O2 requires exactly 3.6 L of water and 19.2 kWh of electrical energy (6.0 kWh/kg).
simplificationRationale: Preserves exact chemical mass conservation: without water and electricity, oxygen generation is chemically impossible.

title: Exploration Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) Water Recovery
authorOrMission: NASA ISS Program (Exploration ECLSS WPA & Brine Processor Assembly)
measuredFact: NASA exploration ECLSS architecture establishes an initial baseline target of approximately 90% water recovery. In 2023, the ISS achieved a historic 98% water recovery milestone using the catalytic Water Processor Assembly combined with the Brine Processor Assembly (BPA).
gameAssumption: Artemis Base Alpha begins with an 80% water recovery efficiency, upgradeable to 90% (Level 2) and up to 99% (Level 3).
simplificationRationale: Allows commanders to experience the critical operational gap between low recycling (fast water depletion) and closed-loop mastery.

title: Orion Artemis I Cislunar Radiation Environment Flight Measurements
authorOrMission: NASA Human Research Program / HERA & MARE Experiments
measuredFact: Active sensors inside the uncrewed Orion spacecraft during Artemis I measured a Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) dose-equivalent rate of 0.96–1.24 mSv/day in cislunar and lunar orbit. (Context: These were measured inside Orion in transit/orbit, not directly on the lunar surface).
gameAssumption: Nominal surface background dose is set to 1.00 mSv/day as a game assumption inspired by the Artemis I data. Solar storms add +15 to +35 mSv. Linear shielding attenuation (1 - shielding) is a simplified educational gameplay model.
simplificationRationale: Provides a realistic radiation risk order of magnitude without requiring complex Monte Carlo particle transport and secondary neutron backscatter simulations.

title: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Diviner Radiometer Surface Illumination Data
authorOrMission: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / UCLA
measuredFact: The Moon has a synodic day of ~29.53 Earth days. In non-polar terrain, a surface outpost experiences approximately 14.75 Earth days (354 hours) of solar daylight followed by 14.75 Earth days (354 hours) of total darkness, with surface temperatures dropping below -130°C.
gameAssumption: A 30-day lunar mission features Daylight on Days 1–14, an integer 14 Earth days (336 hours) of Lunar Night on Days 15–28, and Dawn on Days 29–30.
simplificationRationale: Discretizes the 354-hour lunar night into integer 24-hour simulation turns (336 hours) to confront students with energy storage dilemmas.

title: LCROSS Impact Confirmation of Lunar South Pole Volatiles and Water Ice
authorOrMission: NASA Ames Research Center / Science Magazine (Colaprete et al., 2010)
measuredFact: The Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) impacted the permanently shadowed region (PSR) of Cabeus crater, detecting water vapor estimating approximately 5.5% ± 1.5% (approx. 6%) water ice by mass in the ejecta plume. Cabeus is situated ~120 km from Shackleton Crater.
gameAssumption: Artemis Base Alpha is sited at the Shackleton Crater rim. LCROSS confirmed volatile ice in Cabeus, providing regional scientific foundation for locating an outpost near South Pole cold traps.
simplificationRationale: Clearly distinguishes Cabeus (impact discovery site) from Shackleton (outpost location), while explaining the geological linkage.

title: NASA Veggie and Advanced Plant Habitat (APH) Space Crop Production Investigations
authorOrMission: NASA Kennedy Space Center / ISS Space Biology
measuredFact: The ISS Veggie production system accommodates 6 plant pillows for microgravity salad-crop investigations. The Advanced Plant Habitat (APH) is an automated enclosed research facility supporting extended experiments up to 135 days (e.g., dwarf wheat, chile peppers).
gameAssumption: Hydroponic greenhouse modules produce +4.0 kg fresh biomass food/day, consuming 6 kWh electrical power and 16 L water/day. This represents fresh wet biomass, not dry edible grain, and is an educational game assumption not scaled from Veggie/APH.
simplificationRationale: Simulates agricultural balance where crops provide ongoing caloric production while imposing non-trivial water and electrical loads.

title: Human Exploration of Mars Design Reference Architecture 5.0
measuredFact: Mars orbits at ~1.52 AU from the Sun, reducing solar irradiance to ~590 W/m² (approximately 43.3% of Earth/Moon's 1361 W/m²). Atmospheric dust storms significantly increase optical depth (tau), reducing surface solar power by up to 80%.
gameAssumption: Mars campaign solar generation yields 32 kWh/sol (compared to 45 kWh/day on the Moon). This 71.1% generation ratio reflects a larger deployed photovoltaic array surface area to compensate for the lower 43.3% solar irradiance.
simplificationRationale: Accurately conveys the 43.3% solar irradiance deficit at 1.52 AU while explaining why surface outpost power arrays must be larger.
